about: The mutant ledger of runtime/v1: edits of the runtime's source (runtime/v1 and the runtime/rt clock it parks on) that some runtime/v1 test must kill. Run it with go run ./scripts/mutants ./runtime/v1; the runner judges it by runtime/v1's own tests (docs/tooling.md, "Mutant ledger"). Seeded in batch 14 from the mutants batch 13 killed by hand (fua-b round 2 and its verifier, /home/exedev/.cache/baton/wf10/batch-13/verify/verdicts-2.md).

mutants.name: l10b-shrink-no-adjacent
mutants.rule: After the binary search, adjacent decrements reach a local minimum.

mutants.name: l10b-shrink-linear-search
mutants.rule: Monotone integer shrinking reaches the boundary with logarithmically bounded replay work.

mutants.name: b13-drain-unparked
mutants.rule: runtime.md Machines and actors 11.16: a member's Drain of an actor waits parked.

mutants.rule: runtime.md Machines and actors 11.16: an Ask's or a State's wait for the answer is parked.

mutants.name: b13-exitof-unparked
mutants.from: func (a *Actor[S, E, D]) waitDone(t *rt.Task) { a.waitEnd(t, t.Done()) }
mutants.rule: runtime.md Machines and actors 11.16: ExitOf's wait for the actor's end is parked.

mutants.to:

mutants.rule: runtime.md Machines and actors 11.16: a Send's wait for room in a full mailbox is parked.

mutants.name: b13-advancing-check-removed
mutants.rule: runtime.md 16: one Advance of a clock runs at a time; a second is a defect in its caller, not a wait.

mutants.name: b14-settle-hostget
mutants.rule: stdlib.md actor 7 Hosts, runtime.md 11.16: a Host.Get waiting on an empty host is parked.

mutants.name: b14-settle-nested-advance
mutants.rule: runtime.md 11.16: a task's Wait for another task is parked, so the task it waits for may Advance the clock.

mutants.name: e4b-client-timeouts-unchecked
mutants.rule: Shared Limits rejects a non-positive timeout at NewClient too.

mutants.name: e4b-network-timeouts-unchecked
mutants.rule: Shared Limits rejects a non-positive timeout even for an empty network policy.

mutants.name: cu6-budget-ignored
mutants.rule: A streamed body over MaxBodyBytes fails TooLarge; the budget bounds what a sink is given.

mutants.name: cu6-declared-length-ignored
mutants.rule: A declared Content-Length over the budget fails TooLarge before any part reaches the sink.

mutants.name: cu6-redirect-body-streamed
mutants.from: follow := func(r HTTPResponse) bool { return hops != -1 && httpLocation(r) != "" }
mutants.to: follow := func(r HTTPResponse) bool { return false }
mutants.rule: The body of a redirect that is followed never reaches the sink.

mutants.name: cu6-partial-file-kept
mutants.rule: A failed or stopped FetchFile leaves no new file.

mutants.name: cu6-rename-skipped
mutants.from: if err := root.root.Rename(file.tmp, name); err != nil {
mutants.rule: A FetchFile that succeeds leaves the whole body at its path and nothing beside it.

mutants.name: cu6-stream-not-joined
mutants.rule: A stop mid-body cancels the exchange, so the peer sees the hang-up before the call ends.

mutants.name: cu6-stop-ignored
mutants.rule: A stop of the caller ends a streamed fetch that waits for its next part.

mutants.name: cu6b-status-ignored
mutants.rule: A body reaches the sink only for a status the caller accepts; any other is StatusRefused.

mutants.name: cu6b-prefix-unbounded
mutants.rule: StatusRefused's Prefix holds at most httpPrefixBytes of the body.

mutants.name: cu6b-prefix-dropped
mutants.rule: StatusRefused's Prefix is the body's first bytes, for a message.

mutants.name: cu6b-eager-file
mutants.from:
file := &BodyFile{root: root, name: name}
	kept := false
mutants.rule: IntoFile makes no new file before the first part: a refused status touches no file.

mutants.name: cu6b-open-failure-lost
mutants.rule: A new file that cannot be made fails with its fs failure, not SinkFailed.

mutants.name: cu6b-empty-file-skipped
mutants.rule: An accepted empty body still leaves an empty file at the path.

mutants.name: cu6b-fixed-follows
mutants.from: func(HTTPResponse) bool { return false }, accepts, put)
mutants.to: func(r HTTPResponse) bool { return httpLocation(r) != "" }, accepts, put)
mutants.rule: The fixed-origin client follows no redirect: a 307 is a final response whose status meets the rule.

mutants.name: cu6b-fixed-accepts-lost
mutants.from: func(HTTPResponse) bool { return false }, accepts, put)
mutants.to: func(HTTPResponse) bool { return false }, func(int) bool { return true }, put)
mutants.rule: The fixed-origin client applies the caller's accepted statuses.

mutants.name: cu5-zone-not-escaped
mutants.rule: A canonical origin remains a parseable URL, including an escaped IPv6 interface zone, so a credential owner can be read again.

mutants.name: cu5-default-port-not-normalized
mutants.rule: An origin uses its effective numeric port; zero-padded default ports denote the same origin.

mutants.name: cu5-zone-case-folded
mutants.rule: IPv6 interface-zone identities are not DNS names and retain their case.

mutants.name: cu5-policy-bypassed
mutants.rule: The initial and each redirect origin must satisfy the stated policy before any exchange.

mutants.name: cu5-credential-leaks
mutants.rule: A credential reaches only its own origin, including when two origins have the same hostname but different ports.

mutants.name: cu5-extra-hop
mutants.rule: Follow's MaxHops is an exact maximum of followed redirects, including zero.

mutants.name: cu5-no-redirects-ignored
mutants.rule: NoRedirects returns the redirect response without following or refusing its first hop.

mutants.name: cu5-caller-lost
mutants.from: httpDoURL(t, u, limits, method, fields, body)
mutants.to: httpDoURL(rt.Root("lost caller"), u, limits, method, fields, body)
mutants.rule: A stop cancels and joins the current exchange even after a redirect; the target peer sees the hang-up.

mutants.name: rpc-calls-stop
mutants.rule: A stopped caller's Loopback Call (or a stopped request) ends with the stop, not with a defect read from an Interrupt exit, and after the call's release ran.

mutants.name: rpc-calls-join
mutants.rule: A failed emit (a WriteFailed of the ndjson stream) stops every call of the batch still held and waits for its release before RPCExitLines returns; no call outlives its request. (A stop of the request also reaches each call by the task tree, so TestRPCCallsStopWithTheCaller does not catch this.)

mutants.name: r3b-local-exit
mutants.rule: A Loopback Call reads the json Exit its server answered; the contract's laws hold through it.
killers: examples:limiter/loopback (ergo test: limits.Limiter laws for Loopback)

mutants.to: reopened, err := os.OpenRoot(r.root.Name()); if err != nil { return fsErr(path, err) }; defer reopened.Close(); if err := f(reopened); err != nil {
mutants.rule: A Root retains the opened directory across a rename and replacement of its name.

mutants.name: root-release-omitted
mutants.rule: Every acquired Root closes at frame end, including failure, defect and stop.

mutants.name: stream-flush
mutants.rule: Each streamed Write reaches the client before it returns.

mutants.name: stream-second-answer
mutants.rule: A streamed response is the stream alone; the handler's result after it is not sent.

mutants.name: stream-late-write
mutants.from:
defer x.mu.Unlock()
	x.ended = true
	return x.started
mutants.rule: A writer kept past its request fails WriteFailed; it never writes to a finished response.

mutants.name: stream-stop-check
mutants.from:
func (x *Exchange) Write(t *rt.Task, text string) error {
	t.Check()
mutants.rule: A hang-up stops the request task, and the writer's next Write ends with that stop.

mutants.name: http-header-budget
mutants.rule: The required header budget configures the HTTP parser rather than silently using another cap.

mutants.name: http-body-budget
mutants.rule: A body over the required limit is a typed body value, not a partial body.

mutants.name: http-empty-content-type
mutants.rule: An empty response has no content type.

mutants.name: http-swaps-fields
mutants.rule: Buffered headers and repeated query values retain their names and text.

mutants.name: http-truncated-body
mutants.rule: A half-closed input still delivers the typed read refusal.

mutants.name: http-serial-handlers
mutants.rule: Independent requests run concurrently; one blocked handler does not block admission of every other handler.

mutants.name: http-disconnect-ignored
mutants.rule: A client abort stops its handler task and drains its cleanup.

mutants.name: http-idle-unbounded
mutants.rule: A kept-alive connection that waits IdleTimeout for its next request is closed.

mutants.name: http-body-budget-swapped
mutants.rule: Each read phase is bounded by its own Limits timeout.

mutants.name: http-header-not-after-idle
mutants.rule: The next request's header is bounded from its first byte.

mutants.name: http-body-expiry-closes
mutants.rule: An expired body reaches the handler as a failed read, and its answer is sent.

mutants.name: http-idle-limit-unchecked
mutants.rule: A zero or negative timeout is InvalidLimits, never an unbounded phase.

mutants.name: http-stop-leaves-timers
mutants.rule: A Serve that ends on a defect stops and drains every phase timer first.

mutants.name: http-timers-overlap
mutants.to: pt.h.Task().Interrupt(); if pt.c.timer == pt { pt.c.timer = nil }
mutants.rule: A connection has at most one live phase timer task: its old timer must be joined, not merely interrupted, before the next starts.

mutants.name: client-body-budget
mutants.rule: A response body over the client's budget is TooLarge, never a truncated success.

mutants.name: client-query-order
mutants.rule: Query values arrive as sent: each is escaped once.

mutants.name: client-follows-redirects
mutants.rule: One request is one exchange: a 3xx comes back as sent.

mutants.name: client-path-raw
mutants.rule: Path is the decoded path: the client escapes it, so it arrives as sent.

mutants.name: client-refused-kind
mutants.rule: A refused connection is the typed Refused cause, apart from a broken exchange.

mutants.name: client-stop-ignored
mutants.rule: A stop of the caller cancels the exchange and ends the call with the stop.

mutants.name: rchk-refused-die
mutants.rule: A Die named RpcError (the server's rpc layer could not read the call) is the typed Transport for a client, not the server's defect (rpc.md, Call).
